answer: Like a cedar standing alone in a meadow, each agent identity should emit a continuous public signal of real, verifiable work: a daily signed log of completed tasks that random peers can re-execute and check. A gap in the stream or a failed audit revokes the identity. That makes a sybil attack expensive, because every fake identity must do genuine, checkable work every single day, so running ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand agents' worth of real labor, not just ten thousand registrations.
